subject: ventures/ci-test-shard-balancer
professional: a senior build/CI infrastructure engineer who owns test parallelism for a large monorepo (the person who would otherwise use CircleCI `tests split --split-by=timings`, pytest-split, jest --shard or Knapsack); first checks: does the union of the emitted shard commands run every test exactly once, does the predicted slowest shard match what those commands will actually run, is the partition really near-optimal, are real runner reports (not hand-written fixtures) parsed right, and does the CI gate measure the split the pipeline actually runs

evidence.correctness: The partitioner is right: my own exhaustive enumerator (scratchpad brute.mjs, n^m assignments, own PRNG, imports only balance/lpt) over 600 random instances (2-4 shards, 3-10 units, uniform/integer/log-normal times) found balance() never above the true optimum, never flagged 'optimal' wrongly, all units placed exactly once, and LPT within Graham's 4/3-1/(3n) bound (worst ratio 1.1667). Real runner output parses right: a pytest 9.1.1 --junitxml from a suite I wrote gives file sums 1.002/0.852/0.805/0.502 s by hand, best 3-way makespan 1.307 s, tool prints 1.307; for --group file and --group test the emitted pytest commands, run with --collect-only, select exactly the 11 tests of the full suite. A real gotestsum v1.12.0 report collapses TestTable/x,y,z into TestTable (0.6 s) and running the emitted `go test -run '^(...)$'` commands with -v runs exactly the 5 top-level tests. But outputs are wrong in documented modes: (1) pytest --group class emits the bare file for module-level tests, so `pytest tests/unit/test_math.py` on shard 1 also runs TestMul, which shard 2 runs again: 4 tests run twice and shard 1 really takes about 1.66 s, not the predicted 1.153 s; (2) Jest and RSpec with --group test (the tool's own advice for a bottleneck file) emit whole file paths, so on fixtures/jest.xml shard 2's `npx jest src/cart/cart.test.ts src/search/search.test.ts src/util/util.test.ts` runs the whole 40.5 s suite against a predicted 10.4 s, and every file runs on two or three shards; (3) the same Go report passed twice (or a gotestsum --rerun-fails report) inflates TestTable to 1.2 s because subtest times are summed across duplicates before the max, contradicting the README's 'duplicates count once at their longest time'. Core default path right, three wrong-output modes: 2.
evidence.completeness: Checked each README bullet. Reads: pytest and Go verified on real runner output; Jest, Maven, RSpec only on the author's fixtures (no network jest-junit/surefire run here). Balances with LPT + local search + exact B&B and reports optimality: verified. Shows current vs balanced, wall-clock, billed, savings, --runs-per-month: verified on fixtures/pytest.xml (41.0/30.4 s current, 38.2/33.2 s balanced, 2.4 -> 2.3 min). Sweeps and recommends: works. Flags the indivisible bottleneck and suggests --group test: works (but see correctness for Jest/RSpec). Emits commands and --matrix: works for file grouping in all dialects and test grouping in pytest/Go/Java; wrong for pytest class grouping and Jest/RSpec test/class grouping. Gate --max-imbalance-pct exits 1: works mechanically, measures the wrong split without --current-from-reports. Page loads engine.mjs and usage.mjs, has disclaimer and opt-out. No stubs or TODOs. A generated 6,000-test suite splits into 12 shards with --group test --matrix in 0.44 s.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs' (Node 22.23.5): 65 tests, 65 pass, 0.44 s. Six seeded mutants with quality_mutate.py: Go collapse max -> sum caught; dedupe longest -> shortest caught; billed-minutes formula caught; B&B room bound x1.2 caught; knee threshold 1.05 -> 1.25 SURVIVED (the recommended shard count is untested); pytest class-group emitter collapsed to bare file paths SURVIVED. No test runs or inspects the emitted commands for class/test grouping in pytest, Jest or RSpec, which is exactly where the real defects are; the brute-force optimum tests are good.
evidence.craft: Read engine.mjs (646 lines), cli.mjs (177), index.html script, the test files. Clean, deterministic, zero-dependency, sensible module split (engine shared by page and CLI), careful parsing (CDATA/comments stripped, entities decoded, ',' in times). Defects: emitShard silently ignores `group` for Jest and RSpec (engine.mjs:463-470) instead of refusing or emitting name filters; pytest class emitter mixes file and class node ids that overlap (engine.mjs:459); collapseGo sums children across duplicate observations (engine.mjs:171-172); pytestParts treats the first capitalised dotted segment as the class, so a capitalised package directory (tests.API.test_x) becomes path 'tests.py' (engine.mjs:118). Gate silently compares against a synthetic split.
evidence.claims: Checked 9 claims. Backed: 5 dialects read (fixtures + my real pytest/Go runs); LPT/local search/exact and the optimal flag (brute force); billed model N x (slowest + setup) stated with its limit; 'no network call, no randomness' (engine has no fetch/Math.random; same output on rerun); bottleneck flag; not affiliated with Knapsack Pro; commands 'not executed against a live pipeline' disclosed; disclaimer and DNT/opt-out present; served llms.txt/sitemap clean per served-copy.mjs. Not backed: (1) README:35 and index.html:130 say the gate fails when 'your current split' drifts, but with one merged report it measures a name-order equal-count split nobody runs: fixtures/suite-24-files.xml --max-imbalance-pct 20 exits 1 at 42.7% even for a pipeline already running the balanced split, so the gate can never pass for the tool's own users; (2) README 'Duplicate test ids ... count once at their longest time' is false for Go subtests (above); (3) README:9-13 says the alternative 'used to mean guessing ..., or paying for a test-splitting service', omitting the free timing-based splitters (CircleCI tests split --split-by=timings, pytest-split, split-test) a CI engineer already knows.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job as a CI engineer on pytest and on Go: export JUnit, run split with --shards 3, paste the matrix and commands. For file grouping it gives a correct, near-optimal split in under a second, with a sensible shard-count sweep priced on setup time, and the commands select every test exactly once (verified with real pytest --collect-only and go test -v). The job breaks for the case that motivates splitting finer: a Jest or RSpec team told to try --group test gets commands that run whole files on several shards, which makes CI slower than before, and a pytest team using --group class runs tests twice. The gate cannot be used as advertised without per-shard reports. Usable for the common file-level job; 3.
evidence.domain: Multiway number partitioning with LPT, pairwise move/swap improvement and a seeded branch-and-bound with symmetry pruning is a stronger method than the greedy timing split CircleCI and pytest-split use, and the indivisible-unit floor and setup-cost sweep are what a CI engineer reasons about. Departures a practitioner would flag: Jest/RSpec test-level sharding needs name filters (jest -t / rspec -e or file:line), not file lists; no per-file process/collection overhead model beyond per-shard setup; static split with no variance margin (disclosed); the gate should compare against the shards actually run.

defects.what: Jest and RSpec ignore the grouping when emitting commands: with --group test (the tool's own advice for a bottleneck file) or --group class, each shard gets whole file paths, so a file whose tests were spread over several shards runs in full on each of them. fixtures/jest.xml, 3 shards, --group test: shard 2 is `npx jest` on all three files (40.5 s of tests) against a predicted 10.4 s. The predicted split and savings are wrong and CI gets slower.

pytest --group class emits a bare file path for a file's module-level tests, which also selects every class in that file, so those classes run on two shards. Real pytest 9.1.1 run: shard 1 `pytest tests/integration/test_http.py tests/unit/test_math.py` also collects TestMul (4 tests) that shard 2 runs as tests/unit/test_math.py::TestMul; shard 1 takes about 1.66 s, not the predicted 1.153 s.

--max-imbalance-pct without --current-from-reports measures a synthetic equal-count name-order split, not the pipeline's split, yet README and the page say it fails when 'your current split' drifts. A team that already runs the balanced split and gates on its merged report fails forever (suite-24-files.xml: 42.7%, exit 1).

No test inspects emitted commands for class/test grouping in pytest, Jest or RSpec, or the recommended shard count: seeded mutants collapsing pytest class args to files (engine.mjs:459) and widening the knee threshold 1.05 -> 1.25 (engine.mjs:426) both survive 65 tests.

collapseGo takes the max of parent observations but sums child observations across duplicates, so a Go report passed twice or with gotestsum --rerun-fails doubles a parent with subtests (TestTable 0.6 -> 1.2 s), contradicting the README's 'duplicates count once at their longest time'.
pytestParts takes the first capitalised dotted segment as the class, so a capitalised package directory (classname tests.API.test_x) maps to path 'tests.py' and emits an invalid node id.

README frames the alternative as guessing or 'paying for a test-splitting service' and the site compares only to Knapsack Pro; free timing-based splitters a CI engineer would reach for first (CircleCI tests split --split-by=timings, pytest-split, split-test) are not mentioned.

verdict: The partitioning engine is genuinely good: an independent exhaustive enumerator over 600 random instances never beat it and never caught a false 'optimal' flag, LPT stays within Graham's bound, and on real runner output (a pytest 9.1.1 --junitxml and a gotestsum v1.12.0 report I generated) it computes the right file sums (3-shard makespan 1.307 s by hand and by tool) and emits pytest and go commands that, when actually collected or run, select every test exactly once. It misses the bar on correctness, claims and tests because the emitted commands are wrong in documented modes: Jest and RSpec with --group test or class emit whole files, so a file runs on several shards (fixtures/jest.xml shard 2 runs the whole 40.5 s suite against a predicted 10.4 s), and pytest --group class runs a file's classes twice. The CI gate, advertised as catching drift in 'your current split', measures a synthetic name-order split unless per-shard reports are given, so it fails forever for a team already using the balanced split. Two of six seeded mutants survive, both in the emitter/recommendation paths the tests never inspect. For file-level splitting on any of the five runners it is usable today.
